understand.concept: ctype.h declares character classification and case-conversion functions. Each argument must be EOF or representable as unsigned char. Passing a negative plain char value other than EOF is undefined behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: The unsigned-char precondition is essential when processing arbitrary byte values on implementations where char is signed.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: getchar returns int so EOF can be represented separately. Each non-EOF input value is converted to unsigned char before classification.

practise.guidedTask: Explain why getchar returns int and why the cast occurs after the EOF check.
practise.independentTask: Write a function that counts alphabetic, digit and whitespace characters without violating ctype argument rules.
hints: Check EOF before converting the input value to unsigned char.
ctype functions are locale-sensitive and classify single-byte characters, not arbitrary Unicode code points.
Use the return value as a truth value rather than assuming it equals one.
